title: Biodiversity and Endangered Species
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Biodiversity and Endangered Species Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Biodiversity at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels; high biodiversity makes ecosystems stable; threats to species (habitat loss, overhunting, pollution, invasive species); endangered Philippine species and their protection. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 3: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Life Science): levels of biodiversity, threats to species, endangered Philippine species and protecting biodiversity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: More species make an ecosystem more stable.
key_sub: Habitat loss is the biggest threat to species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of life: genetic diversity within a species, species diversity, and ecosystem diversity. Ecosystems with high biodiversity recover better from changes. The Philippines is a megadiverse country with many endemic species.

Many species are endangered by habitat destruction, overhunting and illegal trade, pollution and invasive species. The Philippine eagle, tamaraw, dugong and pangolin need protection. Protected areas, laws, captive breeding and community action help conserve them.

Example

Which is endemic to Mindoro?

A small buffalo

Answer: the tamaraw

Example

Biggest threat to the Philippine eagle?

Its home

Answer: loss of forest habitat

Common mistakes

  • Thinking endangered means extinct.
  • Thinking one species does not matter to an ecosystem.
  • Thinking zoos alone can save species.

items.q: What is a wildlife corridor?

a fence that keeps animals in
items.e: Corridors help populations stay connected.

items.q: Why should you not release a pet turtle or fish into a pond?
c: It will always die right away.
It is good for the pond.
It could become invasive or spread disease.
items.e: Non-native pets can harm local species.

items.q: When comparing solutions, what is a constraint?
c: a limit such as cost, time or space
items.e: Constraints limit possible solutions.

items.q: What does the species–area relationship of Alexander von Humboldt state?
c: species richness increases with area, but only up to a limit
items.e: log S = log C + Z log A.

items.q: What does ‘ecosystem services’ mean?
c: the number of species in an ecosystem
money paid to visit a national park
the benefits people get from ecosystems, such as clean water, pollination and food
items.e: Mangroves protect coasts and act as fish nurseries.

items.q: What is species richness?
c: the number of different species in an area
how evenly individuals are spread among species
items.e: Richness counts species; evenness compares their numbers.

items.q: How does species diversity change from the equator to the poles?
c: it is highest at the poles
items.e: The tropics are the richest.

items.q: What is the most species-rich group of animals?
items.e: More than 70% of all recorded animal species.

items.q: What is species diversity?
c: the number of individuals of one species
the variety of alleles in a population
the number of species in an area and how evenly the individuals are spread among them
the variety of ecosystems in a region
items.e: Species diversity takes in richness and evenness.

items.q: Which population is most at risk from a new disease?
c: a large population with many alleles
a population of a widespread species
a small, inbred population with low genetic diversity
items.e: Tasmanian devils have low genetic diversity, which helped facial tumor disease spread.

items.q: What is genetic diversity?
c: the number of individuals in a population
the variety of habitats in a region
the number of different species in an area
the variety of alleles and genes within a species
items.e: Genetic diversity is variation inside one species.

items.q: What does the 'rivet popper' hypothesis say?
c: losing species is like removing rivets from a plane: losing key ones can make the ecosystem collapse
items.e: Proposed by Paul Ehrlich.

items.q: What does the IUCN Red List record?
c: the conservation status of species and those threatened with extinction
items.e: Updated regularly.

items.q: What is ecosystem diversity?
c: the number of species in one quadrat
the variety of alleles in one species
the size of the largest ecosystem
the variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes in a region
items.e: A region with reef, mangrove and seagrass has high ecosystem diversity.

items.q: Tasmanian devils have very low genetic diversity. Why has this made devil facial tumor disease worse?
c: low diversity makes them grow too fast
their immune systems do not recognize tumor cells from other devils as foreign
the disease is caused by a mutation in the climate
items.e: Similar genes mean the tumor cells are not rejected.

items.q: What is species evenness?
c: how similar the population sizes of the different species are
the total biomass of the community
the number of individuals of the rarest species
items.e: A community where one species dominates has low evenness.

items.q: Which is an ecosystem service of mangroves?
c: protecting coastlines from erosion and providing nurseries for fish
producing most of the oxygen for cities
items.e: Mangrove roots trap sediment and shelter young fish.

items.q: What are sacred groves?
c: forest patches protected by local communities for religious reasons
items.e: Found in Meghalaya, Rajasthan, the Western Ghats and elsewhere.

items.q: Why is high genetic diversity important to a population?
c: some individuals are more likely to survive a new disease or change
it increases the population's size immediately
items.e: Variation is the raw material for natural selection.

items.q: What is biodiversity?
c: the number of animals in an area
the total mass of plants in an ecosystem
the variety of life at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels
the number of endangered species in a country
items.e: Biodiversity includes genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.

items.q: Two sites each have 5 species. At site An each species has about 20 individuals; at site B one species has 90 and the rest have 2 or 3. Which is more diverse?
c: site B, because dominance means a healthier community
site B, because it has more individuals of one species
site A, because it has the same richness and higher evenness
they are equally diverse because richness is the same
items.e: Same richness, higher evenness = higher diversity.

items.q: Why was the Nile perch harmful in Lake Victoria?
c: it led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish
items.e: An example of alien species invasion.

items.q: What is co-extinction?
c: the birth of a new species
the extinction of a species that depends on another species that has become extinct
items.e: e.g. a parasite dying with its host.

items.q: Which change could cause this: Frogs and newts lose their habitat.
c: Bird boxes are put up in a wood.
Trees in a rainforest are cut down.
A pond is filled in to build a parking lot.
items.e: Match the cause to the effect.

items.q: Litter is dropped in a park. Is this a natural change or a change caused by people?
c: a change caused by the Moon
items.e: Some changes happen naturally; others are caused by human activity.

items.q: Fertilizer runs off fields into a lake. What is the most likely effect on living things?
c: More birds have safe places to nest.
Algae grow fast and fish can die from lack of oxygen.
Birds and small mammals get shelter and food.
Animals such as orangutans lose their homes and food.
items.e: Changes to a habitat change what can live there.

items.q: A factory pours waste into a river. Is this a natural change or a change caused by people?

Baby sea turtles walk toward the lights instead of the ocean.
Birds and squirrel lose their homes and food.
Fish and frogs get sick and die.
items.e: Changes in the environment can harm the plants and animals that live there.

items.e: The passenger pigeon is extinct.

items.q: Which is a cause of species becoming endangered?
c: habitat destruction, overhunting, pollution and invasive species
items.e: Habitat loss is the biggest cause.

items.q: Plastic litter is left on a beach. Is this change good for wildlife or harmful to wildlife?
c: it has no effect at all
items.e: People can harm habitats, but they can also protect and improve them.

items.q: How do wildlife sanctuaries help endangered species?
c: they protect habitats where species can live and breed safely
items.e: Protected areas reduce threats.

items.q: What is an ecosystem service?

items.q: Which is the national bird of the Philippines and is critically endangered?
items.e: Fewer than 400 pairs remain in the wild.

items.q: Vincent's class reads: “Farm fields replace a grassland. Bees and butterflies lose flowers to feed on.” Which solution would help most?

items.e: This solution fixes the problem the change caused.

items.q: Which small wild buffalo is found only on Mindoro and is critically endangered?
items.e: The tamaraw is endemic to Mindoro.

items.q: Which law protects wildlife in the Philippines?

items.e: It bans hunting and trading of protected species.

items.q: What does 'critically endangered' mean?
c: a species has already died out

items.e: The IUCN Red List uses this category.

items.q: Why is biodiversity important for people?

items.e: Many medicines come from plants.

items.q: Lava cools into new bare rock. Lichens grow first. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: A glacier melts back and leaves bare rock. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: Which place or event is a place with sacred groves?
items.e: Khasi and Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya: a place with sacred groves.

items.q: Too many fish are caught each year. Which human impact is this?
